ai.title: Disable mirror-dot-agents workflow steps
ai.summary: Commented out the 'Clear default GitHub auth header', 'Configure Git', and 'Push subtree' steps in `.github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml`. This action was taken because the workflow was reportedly blocking deployments, specifically for the web environment. The change is isolated to the CI configuration and does not affect core application logic or user-facing features.

eli5.text: The system stopped running an automated process that used to push a set of starter assistants to a separate shared location every time code was deployed. Deployments to the web environment should now no longer be paused or delayed by that background syncing step. The three specific steps that were removed were clearing a temporary authentication header, setting up the identity of the automated process, and pushing the updated files to the shared location.

ai.title: Lite mode optimization: reduced thinking and agent spawning
ai.summary: The `base-lite` agent configuration was updated to use `openai/gpt-5-chat` and explicitly restrict spawnable agents to `file-explorer`, `file-picker`, `web-researcher`, `docs-researcher`, and `context-pruner`, removing the `reviewer` and `thinker` agents. The `base` factory function now accepts a `mode` argument (`lite`, `normal`, `max`, `experimental`) to dynamically adjust the `instructionsPrompt`. In `lite` mode, the system prompt conditionally omits instructions to spawn the reviewer agent, enforcing a lighter, faster execution path by reducing mandatory agent spawning and thinking overhead.

eli5.text: When you use the lighter, faster version of the assistant, it now skips its usual habit of calling in a second helper to double-check every change, and it leans on a quicker model to think. You'd notice this path completes tasks more directly, without the extra review step, since that step was specifically stripped out for lite mode and nothing else was altered.

ai.title: Fix agent factory type signatures for grok-4 and thinking-base
ai.summary: Updated base() call in .agents/base-experimental.ts to pass 'experimental' mode, and baseAgentUserInputPrompt() in .agents/factory/thinking-base.ts to pass 'normal' mode. Aligns function signatures with required type definitions. Internal type safety fix.

eli5.text: The experimental model and the standard helper now agree on how they're being called, so the system stops tripping over mismatched instructions when it builds its assistant personalities. This only affects how the internal tooling talks to itself today. You wouldn't see it unless you were already poking around the configuration files.

ai.title: Editor step limit raised to 25
ai.summary: Base2 editor step limit raised from 20 to 25. Tool result extraction switched from XML parsing to structured `messageHistory` filtering for `write_file` and `str_replace`. Successful edit detection now relies on absence of `errorMessage` in JSON output rather than string matching.

eli5.text: The assistant can now carry on thinking for five extra steps before it has to pause and summarize its progress, which gives it more room to work through a longer task before stopping. When it finally does pause, the way it gathers up its own edits has changed behind the scenes: instead of reading results out of a text log, it now pulls them from a cleaner, structured record, and it decides an edit worked by checking for the absence of an error flag rather than searching for success words. ai.title: Fix Windows HEREDOC compatibility in git commit commands
ai.summary: System prompt and tool definitions updated to detect platform for `git commit` syntax. HEREDOC (`<<'EOF'`) restricted to Unix/bash; Windows Command Prompt uses direct double-quoted strings. Changes in `backend/src/system-prompt/prompts.ts` and `backend/src/tools/definitions/tool/run-terminal-command.ts` ensure cross-platform commit generation.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to create a git commit, it now checks whether you're on Windows or a Unix-like system (Mac/Linux) and uses the correct command syntax for your platform. Previously, it always used a HEREDOC format (<<'EOF') that works fine on Mac and Linux but breaks on Windows Command Prompt, causing commits to fail. Now, on Windows it switches to a simpler double-quoted string format that works reliably there. The next time you request a commit on a Windows machine, it should succeed instead of stalling on a syntax error.

ai.title: Suppress CLI prompt during paste mode
ai.summary: The CLI now clears the readline prompt via `this.rl.setPrompt('')` when `isPasting` is true, preventing multiple `>` symbols from appearing during multi-line paste operations. The normal prompt is restored by calling `this.setPrompt()` when paste mode ends (detected by `detectPasting` or idle timeout). This fixes a visual display issue in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`.

eli5.text: When you paste several lines of text into the terminal at once, the extra > symbols that used to show up are now hidden until the paste is finished, so the text you pasted no longer mixes with the prompt. The fix is live today for everyone who uses the terminal tool, and it only affects how things look, not how they work.

ai.title: Release 1.0.474 ships lite mode, eval cost tracking, and agent
ai.summary: Version 1.0.474 rolls up user-visible improvements across the agent runtime, SDK, and docs surfaces. Lite mode now restricts the base-lite agent to openai/gpt-5-chat and a reduced spawn set (file-explorer, file-picker, web-researcher, docs-researcher, context-pruner), with the base factory accepting a mode argument that adjusts the instructions prompt. Git evals now capture totalCostUsd and runtime_sec per run and report average_cost_usd and average_runtime_sec, while the judge prompt scopes scoring strictly to the spec and drops efficiency metrics. The SDK ships as a dual ESM/CJS bundle built with Bun, and initial-agents-dir templates now carry an Apache-2.0 LICENSE plus a package.json defining agent metadata.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in npm-app/release/package.json changes the version field from 1.0.473 to 1.0.474, a single-line release-bump commit (stats +1 / -1) tagged as Internal / release-bump with Version bump: 1.0.474 in the analysis notes.

ai.title: mirror-dot-agents.yml enables debug ssh session
ai.summary: Uncomments 'Clear default GitHub auth header' and 'Configure Git' steps in .github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml. Adds 'ssh' step using mxschmitt/action-tmate@v3 with CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN_DOT_AGENTS secret. 15-minute timeout guard included. Internal CI change for debugging deploy blocking issues.

eli5.text: The deployment assistant that syncs code between branches now pauses and opens a direct troubleshooting line when something goes wrong, letting GitHub staff debug the exact moment a deploy gets stuck rather than guessing from logs. This affects only the internal syncing process for the 'dot agents' project and is active immediately; if you monitor those deployments, you'll see a short, time-limited SSH session appear in the workflow whenever it runs. The change un-commented three previously skipped setup steps and added a secure connection step, all wrapped with a 15-minute safety timeout.

ai.title: Restore mirror-dot-agents subtree push
ai.summary: Re-enabled git subtree push in `.github/workflows/mirror-dot-agents.yml`, replacing the temporary `mxschmitt/action-tmate` debug step. Switched secret from `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN_DOT_AGENTS` to `CODEBUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN`. Mirrors `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir` to `codebuffai/codebuff-dot-agents` main.

eli5.text: The automated process that keeps a shared library of helper agents up to date is working again. Previously it had been paused and replaced with a manual debugging setup, so updates were not being published automatically; now it once again pushes changes from the company's main code repository to the public library folder. If you watch that library repository, you will see new files appear automatically after code changes, instead of nothing happening until someone intervenes.

ai.title: Route all gemini calls through openrouter
ai.summary: Gemini model references in backend and common constants switch to OpenRouter equivalents. `fast-rewrite.ts`, `request-files-prompt.ts`, and `get-documentation-for-query.ts` now use `models.openrouter_gemini2_5_flash` instead of direct Gemini IDs. `old-constants.ts` updates `shortModelNames` mappings for `gemini-2.5-pro` and `flash-2.5`. Type signatures in `gemini-with-fallbacks.ts` change from `GeminiModel` to generic `Model`.

eli5.text: The assistant now routes all its Gemini model requests through an intermediary service called OpenRouter instead of talking to Gemini directly. This affects the behind-the-scenes plumbing that handles rewriting, file searching, and documentation lookups, so those features continue to work the same way for you, you won’t notice any difference in the output, but the path the requests take has changed. The change is live today and doesn’ block or slow anything down; it’s a quiet switch in how the system connects to its underlying models.
